claims.content: The System Administrator revises device command safety rules by uploading a new database version to the production system after testing the rule changes in the Simulator environment.

goal.raw_text: The System Administrator revises device command safety rules by uploading a new database version to the production system after testing the rule changes in the Simulator environment.

claims.content: System Administrator
The System Administrator must test the rule changes in the Simulator environment before uploading to the production system.
The System Administrator must prepare a new database version containing the revised rules.
The System Administrator must have the additional login password required for configuring device rules.
The System Administrator decides to change or update the device command safety rules on the production system.

trigger.raw_text: The System Administrator decides to change or update the device command safety rules on the production system.

claims.content: The System Administrator tests the revised device command safety rules in the Simulator environment.
The System Administrator uploads a new database version containing the revised rules to the production system.
The System Administrator provides the additional login password required for configuring device rules.
The system analyzes the data in the database tables for conflicting or redundant entries before storing them.
If the System Administrator uploads a database version with conflicting or redundant entries, the system analyzes the data and notifies the administrator of the conflicts before storing them.

If integrity verification fails during or after uploading revised rules (e.g., hash mismatch), the system generates an alarm condition and prevents the affected control unit from being used in control sequences.
The revised device command safety rules are successfully stored in the production system’s database after being tested in the Simulator environment.
Any conflicting or redundant entries in the uploaded rule set are identified and reported to the System Administrator prior to final storage.
A UTC date/time stamp is appended to the modified rule data as the last step of the update process.
Message Digest (hash) values are computed and stored for the updated rule set to support future integrity verification.
